entry.shape: native mixed plugin: definePluginEntry default export; four api.registerTool version-2 factories ({ contextVersion: 2, create }) registered optional; one api.registerCli root command
entry.manifest: openclaw.plugin.json: id sess, contracts.tools, toolMetadata optional, cliCommands sess, skills ./skills, strict configSchema
importSubpaths: openclaw/plugin-sdk/config-mutation (readConfigFileSnapshotForWrite; loaded lazily inside `openclaw sess setup` only)
hostRuntimeUsed: api.runtime.state.openKeyedStore({ namespace, maxEntries, overflowPolicy: 'reject-new' }).withCurrent({ assertCurrent }) -> observe / compareAndApply / registerIfAbsent / lookup
tool context v2: assertInvocationCurrent, agentId, sessionKey, sessionId; assertMemoryAudienceCurrent when supplied

1_entryAndGuard.evidence: Installed packed plugin loads (plugins inspect --runtime: status loaded, 4 tools, cli sess, diagnostics []); version-2 factory receives assertInvocationCurrent (function) on /tools/invoke calls.

2_identityBinding.binding: exact (agentId, sessionKey, sessionId) from the v2 tool context; sessionKey is compared, never parsed
demonstrated: a different conversation (session key) is refused the same handle (real host)
a different agent or sessionId is refused (unit, fake host)
a call without a host sessionId (unstarted main session) is refused HOST_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE
plugin reload (plugins reload sess) keeps records and re-admits the same binding
host aborts the tool signal when the caller disconnects; polling stops
2_identityBinding.gap: Reset rejection NOT demonstrated: on 2026.10.3 both sessions.reset and a /reset chat command kept sessionId for a transcript-less dashboard session (only lifecycleRevision, which tool contexts do not expose, changed). /tools/invoke supplies no memoryAudience/assertMemoryAudienceCurrent. Host docs state sessionId is regenerated on /new and /reset for chat sessions; the funded agent-turn qualification (agentTurnQualification.items.resetIncarnationRejection_OC18) found that /new keeps sessionId even with a transcript, so OC-18 FAILS on this host. Revocation-mid-wait rejection is unit-tested only.

3_durableState.evidence: Pending record written before a gateway stop was read after restart; the same handle resumed and returned a verified answer. Store is bounded with overflowPolicy reject-new (host-documented non-evicting for new keys); a capacity-pressure run is deferred to G2.

4_privateLinkBeforeWait.evidence: sess_request returns humanUrl in its private tool result before any wait; sess_response performs the wait. G0 (direct invoke) did not qualify early delivery through a chat surface. Later cross-reference: in dashboard (Control UI) agent turns the link reached the conversation before the wait (agentTurnQualification.items.earlyInChatLinkDelivery, PASS); delivery.send is still not used and messaging channels are not qualified.

5_asyncResultTimeoutCancel.evidence: Verified answer returned through the same live sess_response call ~1.3 s after human submission; caller disconnect aborted the tool signal and stopped polling; a 120 s tool call was not cut by the host on /tools/invoke (adapter budget ended it as needs_resume). Agent-turn host tool timeout NOT measured.

6_setupDoctor.evidence: openclaw --help lists sess from manifest metadata. openclaw sess doctor reads config presence and redacted state counts only, prints no secrets and contacts no network. openclaw sess setup previews by default and with --yes applies through the documented public api.runtime.config.mutateConfigFile (afterWrite mode none, never restarts); exercised in the real 2026.10.3 host CLI by check-package --host (preview writes nothing, additive apply keeps existing tools.alsoAllow and unrelated config, idempotent re-run).

qualifiedOnHost.moveCollisionSemantics: PROBED (public plugin-state-store-runtime, temp state): moveEntriesFrom onto an existing destination keeps the destination AND removes the source (returns the source count). The adapter pre-checks destinations, re-reads them after every move and restores any lost source value into active. A destination that is the same record after a concurrent prune (only generation, updatedAt and humanUrl differ) counts as moved, so no stale pre-prune duplicate is restored.

contract.source: adapters/CONTRACT.md (the shared adapter contract in the sess-sdk repository)
contract.answerRelease: After receipt verification, an authenticated current-revision read precedes any answer release; failed read -> unavailable; progress -> blocked; concurrent local change -> conflict; no answer data released (review R-01, tests/unit/r01-r02.test.ts).
contract.resultRelease: The tool execute boundary re-asserts the live invocation lease after every awaited runner (review R-02).

agentTurnQualification.profile: disposable OpenClaw profile; dashboard conversations (Control UI / webchat surface) created with sessions.create; turns run with `openclaw agent --session-key` through the Gateway; cron, heartbeat, utility model, memory-core and bonjour disabled so only explicit turns call the model
agentTurnQualification.hostToolMode: Code Mode: the model reaches plugin tools through the host's catalog bridge (exec + catalog.search), not as direct tools; long tool calls yield and the model awaits them with the host `wait` tool

earlyInChatLinkDelivery.evidence: A1: the assistant message carrying the private link was committed to the conversation before sess_response started; operator reads of chat.history (the Control UI's source) showed the link while the sess_response wait was still blocking (link at 12.6 s, submission at 14.7 s, verified answer in the same turn). B1/C1 also showed the link during their waits.

normalChatContinuation.evidence: A1: verified answer returned through the same live sess_response call. B1 ended needs_resume after a 45 s bounded wait; after the person submitted, the next normal chat turn (B2) called sess_response once and reported the verified link_holder answer in the same conversation.

resetIncarnationRejection_OC18.evidence: On 2026.10.3 a standalone `/new` (and sessions.reset) on a dashboard conversation with a transcript keeps the same sessionId (only lifecycleRevision changes, which tool contexts do not expose). A2 after `/new`: the old handle was still accepted. The adapter binds the host-documented (agentId, sessionKey, sessionId); this host does not rotate sessionId on reset, so reset does not isolate pending SESS work in this profile.

alsoAllowExposure.evidence: `openclaw sess setup --yes` added the four tools to tools.alsoAllow; the model found and called sess_request/sess_response through the Code Mode catalog in every turn (first A1 call used a wrong argument shape and was rejected by schema validation, then retried correctly).

twoSimultaneousConversations.evidence: B1 and C1 ran concurrently with distinct handles; C2 in conversation C using B's handle got NOT_FOUND with no data.

agentTurnQualification.hostToolTimeout: A 45 s sess_response tool call completed (no host cut). In Code Mode the running call yields and the model issues host `wait` calls on the same execution (4 for a 45 s wait, 1 for 20 s); these are extra model calls but not repeated sess_response polling. Each turn made exactly one sess_response call.
